title: Annotatio IV §.XXIII cont.: Wren AD POSTERIUS — Psychics, Barjesuits, Jesuits throw the material-supposit difficulty
pass_a_gloss: To the LATTER the Author continues to reply in n. 3 p. 329 entire, with the following: Nor does anything now twice stand in the way — that which by all the Psychics indeed, the Barjesuits, and the Jesuits as well (for those little foxes are coupled together by this tail of huckstering the Sacrament) is tossed about as the greatest and inescapable difficulty.
pass_b_english: Wren’s AD POSTERIUS (n. 3 p. 329): nothing now blocks twice — the Psychics, Barjesuits, and Jesuits (foxes tied by the same sacrament-huckstering tail) toss this as their greatest inescapable difficulty.
What follows is their material-supposit objection against spiritual participation.
source_text: AD POSTERIUS pergit respondere Autor n. 3. p. 329. integra, sequentibus: Nec quicquam jam bis officit, quod à Psychicis quidem omnibus, Barjesuitis, Jesuitisque; (Una enim copulantur, per hanc Sacramenti cauponandi caudam, vulpeculæ istæ;) pro maxima & ineluctabili difficultate jactitatur.
